findings.title: The 'full-record schema block' test counts address-reviews' worked examples, so the reference holds three blocks, not one
findings.recommendation: The requirement defines a schema block as a JSON block whose top-level keys include `command` and states 'today six blocks across five references'. Measured with that rule on the built templates: review run-summary-schema.md 2, external-handoff.md 1, address-reviews run-summary-schema.md 3, audit-drift 1, archive 1 — EIGHT. Two of address-reviews' three are worked-example blocks ((a) walk-mode clean run and a later example) that carry `command`. Under walk 2's nearest-preceding attachment rule each would owe its own examples and joint key coverage, so task 3.3's single example cannot pass and task 4.2's 'six schema blocks' assertion fails on the real tree. The miscount predates walk 2 (design D1 at propose counted review's two blocks and not address-reviews'); walk 2's attachment rule makes it consequential. Repair the definition and the count together, in the spec, design D1, tasks 3.3 and 4.2, and explore D-rc07b-6.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Keep the `command` rule; task 3.3 removes `command` from address-reviews' worked-example blocks (they are partial illustrations, not full records), so the reference holds ONE schema block and the count stays six — state that worked examples omit `command` by convention.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Define a schema block by its position — the first JSON block under the reference's `## Schema` heading — so worked examples are never schema blocks whatever keys they show; the count stays six and no template edit is needed for classification.

commentary: Verification of walk 2 over its four sweep scopes, then every proposal pass over the same scope. All four resolutions are present, complete and clean: the genre-dependent exemption is stated once, named in the residual and pinned by a scenario; model leaves the equality and is asserted separately; the spine repoint covers all four references with a template-wide grep; the attachment rule is stated with its mutation. The one defect sits underneath S1 rather than in it: the definition of a schema block is a key heuristic that also matches worked examples, and the attachment rule is the first mechanism to make that matter — measured, not reasoned, by running the block rule over the built templates. Also traced: the seeded pass file must be a review emit the trail reader accepts as independent (a fresh-class review-<mode> file at the cited token), and address-reviews' source fields are not trail-validated, so no further seeding is needed. Residual check from the commit adding the external return: the four changed files are exactly the sweep scopes.
